title: Lightning does strike the same place twice, often
body: The saying that lightning never strikes the same place twice is a myth. Lightning tends to hit whatever offers the easiest path to the ground, usually the tallest or most exposed object around, and that doesn’t change after a strike. Across the planet there are about 44 lightning flashes every second, close to 1.4 billion a year, so repeat hits on towers, trees and mountaintops are routine.

slides.heading: Tall targets get hit
slides.text: The Empire State Building in New York is struck by lightning about 23 times a year on average.

slides.heading: Hotter than the Sun
slides.text: A bolt heats the air around it to about 30,000 °C, roughly five times hotter than the Sun’s surface. The air expands explosively, and that’s thunder.

slides.heading: Struck seven times
slides.text: US park ranger Roy Sullivan reportedly survived seven lightning strikes between 1942 and 1977, a feat recognised by Guinness World Records.
